clue.text: Key worker possibly having to pedal

definitions.text: Key worker possibly having to pedal

parts.words: Key worker possibly having to pedal
parts.note: a musician who plays keyboards with the hands and a pedalboard with the feet in church

explanation.surface: An essential worker, perhaps a nurse, who must cycle to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key worker' is the pandemic phrase for an essential worker, and 'pedal' suggests a bicycle; here the keys and pedals belong to a church instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This church musician works manual keyboards and also plays bass notes with foot pedals.

clue.text: Record loot hoarded by rank villain

indicators.note: hoarded by means kept inside the word for rank

parts.note: rank means rate, as in first-rate
EP is an extended-play record
to loot is to rob

explanation.surface: A record of stolen goods stashed by an utter rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' looks like an adjective for the villain; it is the verb rate.
explanation.definitionFit: An unprincipled scoundrel is a villain.

clue.text: Spanish Cheers run dropped from broadcasts

indicators.note: dropped from means the letter for run is taken out of the word for broadcasts

parts.note: to radio is to broadcast
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A Spanish toast whose sprint is cut from the coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is a casual British goodbye, and this is the Spanish farewell.

clue.text: Man a bit hot struggling to receive overs?

definitions.text: Man a bit hot struggling to receive overs?

indicators.note: to receive means the scrambled letters take in the letter for overs
struggling suggests things in disarray, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A cricketer sweltering as he waits to face the bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' puts O into the scramble of MAN A BIT H. In cricket an over is six balls bowled to a batsman. The man is a famous England all-rounder of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Ian Botham, England cricket all-rounder, was a batsman who received overs from bowlers.

clue.text: Implausible bomb might be agreed

parts.note: a tall story is implausible
IED is an improvised explosive device, a roadside bomb

explanation.surface: A far-fetched bomb might have been approved.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures that correspond or match are said to agree, as accounts do.

clue.text: Paltry bite to eat finally snaffled with cunning

indicators.note: the final letter is snaffled, or stolen away, from the word for a bite to eat

parts.note: a bite to eat is a meal
cunning means sly

explanation.surface: A meagre snack, its last morsel craftily pinched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally snaffled' takes the last letter L off MEAL, leaving MEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry and this word both describe something contemptibly small or meagre.

clue.text: Brahmin uses bottles less

indicators.note: bottles means the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A Hindu priest uses fewer bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten less two and ten take away two say the same subtraction.

clue.text: Limb trouble confines poorly animal

parts.note: an arm is a limb

indicators.note: confines means the word for trouble holds the word for poorly inside

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A troublesome sore limb on a sick creature.
explanation.definitionFit: This armour-plated American burrowing mammal is an animal.

clue.text: Dog detailed twice in list

indicators.note: detailed means with its tail cut off, and twice means two final letters go

parts.note: a lurcher is a crossbred hunting dog

explanation.surface: A dog named twice on a register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'list' looks like a register; it is the verb for a ship leaning to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that leans suddenly to one side lists, or tilts.

clue.text: Choice draught has head spinning

indicators.note: the head, the first pair of letters of the word for a draught, is turned round

parts.note: a draught of medicine or magic is a potion

explanation.surface: A potent drink you choose leaves you dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first two letters, PO, are turned round to give OP.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternative you may pick is a choice.

clue.text: Feature youth collecting new and old currency

indicators.note: collecting means the word for youth takes in the letter for new

parts.note: a youth is a lad
the Deutschmark was Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: A young collector gathering coins both modern and obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent feature of a landscape or a turning point is a landmark.

clue.text: Boris eviscerated by his lot after very sad excuses

indicators.note: after places the Boris and party pieces following the word for very

parts.note: very means so

indicators.note: eviscerated means the inside of Boris is removed, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: Boris Johnson's party, the Conservatives, are the Tories

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson gutted by his own party, offering feeble excuses.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson was a Conservative (Tory) Prime Minister of the UK, so 'his lot' is the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Pity-seeking tales told to excuse oneself are sad excuses, an idiom for pleas for sympathy.

clue.text: Silly me having advanced capital in Asia

parts.note: doh is what you say when you realise your own foolishness
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A-level

explanation.surface: Someone admits a blunder after travelling ahead to an Asian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doh!' is Homer Simpson's exclamation, now standard for 'silly me'.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Qatar, on the Persian Gulf in western Asia.

clue.text: Gaudy bit on the side essentially sent packing

indicators.note: the essential, central letter of the word for a bit on the side is sent away

parts.note: a garnish is a decorative bit on the side of a plate

explanation.surface: A flashy lover, dumped at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit on the side' wants to be a lover; it is the garnish on a dish. Its middle letter N is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish and gaudy are synonyms for showy and tastelessly bright.

clue.text: One often up probably wasting money in casino

indicators.note: wasting suggests something ruined or spoiled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler squandering cash in a casino through the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot sleep is often awake through the night.

clue.text: Miserable prior to cargo transfer

parts.note: feeling miserable is feeling down
a cargo is a load

explanation.surface: A gloomy mood before moving goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying a file from a server to your device is a data transfer.

clue.text: Battle to restrain extremely tense car game

indicators.note: to restrain means the word for battle holds something inside

parts.note: battle means war

indicators.note: extremely picks the end letters of tense

parts.note: the Polo is a Volkswagen car

explanation.surface: A fight to hold back a very tense car.
explanation.definitionFit: This pool sport played by swimming teams is a ball game.

clue.text: Translated English at humane learning institute

indicators.note: translated means put into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: English rendered into a humane study centre.
explanation.definitionFit: This classical name, after a temple of Athena, is used by literary and scientific institutions and clubs.

clue.text: Briton dispatched around Champagne regularly

indicators.note: around says the word for dispatched is turned the other way

parts.note: slew, past tense of slay, means killed or dispatched

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of Champagne

explanation.surface: A British traveller sent off on a champagne tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatched' wants to mean sent; it is the past tense of slay, which 'around' turns back to front. 'regularly' takes the even letters of Champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from Wales is one kind of Briton.

clue.text: Bites knight for queen in minor protests

indicators.note: for means the letter for knight replaces the letters for queen

parts.note: quibbles are petty objections
Qu is the abbreviation for queen
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight replacing a queen prompts petty grumbles on the chessboard.
explanation.walkthrough: N replaces QU, the abbreviation for 'queen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Small mouthfuls are bites, as in a nibble of cheese.

clue.text: Perhaps Helen primarily in war-torn city?

definitions.text: Perhaps Helen primarily in war-torn city?

indicators.note: in places those letters within the city's name

parts.note: Troy was besieged for ten years in the Trojan War

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letters of Perhaps and Helen

explanation.surface: Was Helen, above all, a prize in the besieged city?
explanation.walkthrough: Helen of Troy, taken by Paris, was in effect the prize the Trojan War was fought over, so the whole clue defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize won and displayed, as Helen was by Paris in Troy, is a trophy-like possession.

clue.text: Criminal history that is gender-neutral

definitions.meaning: in British slang a person with a criminal record has previous convictions on file
read as ..., female or male, the letters allow either sex

explanation.surface: A criminal record that makes no distinction between the sexes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a pun: split as F OR M, the word offers female or male, so it is gender-neutral. 'Form' for a criminal record is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: British police slang calls a criminal record someone's previous, as in 'he has previous convictions'.

clue.text: Window mounted in abbey exorbitantly

indicators.note: mounted says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words abbey exorbitantly

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A window installed in an abbey at enormous cost.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'mounted' means read upwards, so EYEXO is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A round or oval opening in a building, like a bull's-eye, is a kind of window.

clue.text: Doctor joins ancient crew to stop alien boarding

indicators.note: to stop means to plug, so the pieces fill the gap inside the alien

parts.note: ET is the film alien
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine
Noah's ark men are an ancient ship's crew

explanation.surface: A doctor and an old crew try to block an alien from coming aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The ancient crew are the men of Noah's ark. 'to stop' means to plug a gap, so the doctor and crew fill the alien.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of going aboard a ship or plane is boarding, here as a noun.

clue.text: Ambassador from short space cruise half-cut

parts.note: an en is a printer's space half the width of an em

indicators.note: half-cut means only the first half of the word for cruise is kept

parts.note: a cruise is a voyage

explanation.surface: A diplomat drunk on a brief space cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it trims VOYAGE to VOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic messenger representing a government abroad is an ambassador.

clue.text: Suit could be a little lighter

definitions.meaning: to suit is to go well with, as colours do
a small stick used for making fire, like a lighter

explanation.surface: An outfit that might be paler.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours that go together suit each other; a small fire-starting stick is a little lighter.

clue.text: Old-fashioned veil made to order

indicators.note: made to order suggests something put together freshly, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traditional bridal veil, custom-made.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belonging to the Middle Ages is figuratively hopelessly out of date.

clue.text: Start where French river runs from the east

parts.note: où is French for where

indicators.note: flowing from the east means reading right to left, so the river's name is backwards

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England

explanation.surface: A question of where a French river begins, running west.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a chalk-stream river in Hampshire, southern England, famous for trout fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The very beginning of something is its start.

clue.text: Cross close to short cut by yard

indicators.note: close to means the closing letter of short

parts.note: to etch is to cut lines into a surface

explanation.surface: Something nearly too short is trimmed beside a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Being irritable or bad-tempered is being cross.

clue.text: Some who raved about hospital sample building?

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go round the letter for hospital
raved suggests wild talk, so the letters of Some who are scrambled

explanation.surface: Some visitors gushed about a hospital they viewed.
explanation.definitionFit: On a new estate, a furnished model house shown to buyers is a sample of what is on offer.
